subject: Reserved fleet token velocity audit & sizing
messages:
From: Sam Park <sam.park@neurolytics.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick sizing input for reserved fleet (NeuroLytics)

Hi Irene —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move toward a reserved GPU plan to meet latency and cost targets for our beta. Engineering asked me to get a short pre-sales checklist filled so they can map our token velocity into a committed fleet. Can you send a short questionnaire (or a template) we can fill with realistic traffic numbers?

High-level constraints:
- P99 tail latency target: 450ms for single-shot text generation (prompt + model response)
- Peak burst windows: 10–12 minutes, up to 2x sustained qps
- Must stay within committed monthly spend cap — we may tier up after pilot

I'll attach a small token sample extract (token-sample.csv) and a snippet of session logs. Appreciate anything concise — we want to return this in ~24 hours.

—Sam
Sam Park
Head of DevOps, NeuroLytics
Attachment: token-sample.csv (csv, 12kb); session-logs-snippet.txt (txt, 18kb)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@neurolytics.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick sizing input for reserved fleet (NeuroLytics)

Hi Sam —

Thanks — this is perfect. I took a quick look at the sample and session snippets. To produce a practical reserved-fleet estimate we need a compact questionnaire that maps your request mix to GPU-time. Below is a focused set we use for pre-sales sizing. Can you fill these items? If it's easier I can drop into a collaborative doc and we can pair on numbers.

Required fields (minimal):
1) Traffic profile
   - Avg requests/sec (sustained) and observed peak requests/sec (burst)
   - Percent of requests that are single-turn vs multi-turn sessions (1-turn, 2–5 turns, >5 turns)
2) Prompt/response token distribution
   - Median prompt tokens, 75th, 95th, and max observed prompt tokens
   - Median response tokens, 75th, 95th, and max observed response tokens
3) Concurrency semantics
   - Session affinity required? (yes/no)
   - Average concurrent sessions vs concurrent inferences
4) Quality & latency SLOs
   - Target P50/P95/P99 generation latency (ms) including network to our endpoint
   - Allowed fallback model (if any) when capacity constrained
5) Workload characteristics
   - % KV-cache hit (if you use prefix reuse)
   - % of requests that require tool calls or external I/O
6) Operational constraints
   - Desired commit (monthly tokens or dollars), planned pilot duration
   - Canary plan: % traffic for canary for the first 2 weeks

Optional telemetry dumps: token-sample.csv is great — if you can include a 24–72 hour request-level CSV with timestamps and tokens per request that lets us run a token-velocity audit.

Estimated deliverable and timeline
- We’ll return a first-pass reserved-fleet sketch with sku mix + rough GPU count and expected p99 under your SLO in 24–48 hours after you send answers + the CSV.

If you prefer, Marissa (cc'd) can run the tokenizer audit once we have the CSV and produce a single-sheet estimate. Ben will scope pricing levers (batching, occupancy targets, quantization) to hit your spend cap.

Thanks — I’ll stand by for the CSV.

Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | irene.choi@redwood.ai
From: Sam Park <sam.park@neurolytics.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: devops@neurolytics.io
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick sizing input for reserved fleet (NeuroLytics) — answers attached

Irene — thanks, see answers below and attached a slightly expanded token-sample.csv and a 48h request dump. I included a small column indicating whether the request touched external I/O (db_call=true/false).

Answers (short):
- Avg sustained qps: 25 req/s
- Observed peak qps (10–12 min bursts): 120 req/s
- Request mix: ~70% single-turn, 20% 2–5 turns, 10% >5 turns
- Prompt tokens (median / 75 / 95 / max): 120 / 340 / 980 / 2300
- Response tokens (median / 75 / 95 / max): 60 / 180 / 620 / 1600
- Session affinity: yes (we prefer sticky sessions for chat continuity)
- Concurrent sessions: ~600 active sessions avg; concurrent inferences typically 25 sustained, spikes to ~220
- P50/P95/P99 latency targets: 120ms / 260ms / 450ms (end-to-end)
- Fallback model: we can accept fallbacks to a 4-bit quantized variant if cost/latency trade-off requires it
- KV-cache hit: ~28% (we see moderate prefix reuse for system prompts and persona headers)
- External I/O: ~12% of requests trigger tool/db calls adding 25–300ms to total time
- Commit: pilot target $25k/mo for first 3 months; will reevaluate after. Canary: 5% initial traffic for 2 weeks

Attachments: token-sample.csv (updated, 58kb); inference-sla.pdf; session-logs-snippet.txt

Let us know if any of this needs clarification. Happy to hop on a 30m call.

—Sam
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@neurolytics.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 11:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick sizing input for reserved fleet (NeuroLytics) — first-pass sketch

Sam —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the CSV — that was ideal. High-level notes and a first-pass sketch below. Marissa ran a tokenizer pass and I did a quick token-velocity mapping; Ben added pricing levers.

Observations
- Token velocity: sustained ~25 req/s x median (180 tokens total) ≈ 4.5k tokens/sec sustained (~12.1M tokens/hr). Peak-burst velocity at 120 req/s spikes to ~21.6k tokens/sec for 10–12 minutes.
- Session affinity and 28% KV-cache hit reduce effective per-request compute by roughly 12–18% depending on hit distribution.
- External I/O on 12% of requests increases end-to-end latency but does not change GPU utilization significantly (these calls happen off-GPU).

First-pass reserved-fleet sketch (pilot, $25k/mo target)
- Recommended baseline SKU: 1 x A40-equivalent GPU pool for narrow concurrency experiments is too small. For your SLO and burst shape we recommend a mixed pool: 4 x NVIDIA L40s (or equivalent) with autoscaling headroom of +2 nodes for burst smoothing.
- Expected occupancy target: 55–65% sustained occupancy with continuous batching and prefix KV caching enabled. That occupancy gives you the ~P99 target with continuous batching window tuned to 40–60ms median queueing (keeps tail within 450ms).
- Canary plan: allocate 1 L40 to canary (5% traffic) for first 2 weeks, then ramp to full pool.

Pricing and levers (quick)
- If we allow quantized fallback for >=90% of background traffic, you can reduce GPU-hours by ~18–25% which helps stay within the $25k/mo pilot. Ben will prepare an exact priced option matrix.

Next steps
1) Ben will share a 1-sheet pricing options matrix (2–3 sku mixes + quantization vs no-quant).
2) Marissa will attach the tokenizer audit and a short occupancy simulation (CSV + 3-line readme).
3) Schedule a 30m call this week to review the deck and confirm commit cadence.

Would Thursday 10am PT work to go over the sketch? If not, propose 2 other windows and we’ll book.

Thanks — I’ll add the short deliverables to the HubSpot deal and drop the links (cc: marissa, ben).

Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
